channel.title: The Big Issue - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from The Big Issue (bigissue.com)

item.title: B Corp Month: Food tastes better when it’s served with a conscience
item.description: Our pick of the B Corp-certified food companies balancing purpose and profit with delicious results, from starters to desserts.

item.title: The story of Jews and Muslims' connected history must be told
item.description: Relations between Jews and Muslims span 1,400 years and the spectrum of human interaction, from love and friendship to hate and violence.

item.title: Right to Buy gets a lot of flak, but it was life-changing for me
item.description: While Right to Buy has come under fire for costing councils millions, a Big Issue reader presents a different perspective.

item.title: Big Issue editor Paul McNamee's reflections as he steps down
item.description: Departing Big Issue editor Paul McNamee looks back at his time at the magazine, offers thanks and looks to the future.

item.title: Joining the B Corp movement made Big Issue stronger
item.description: For B Corp Month, Big Issue's impact director Rhys Corley-Morgan explains why certification has been invigorating for Big Issue Group.

item.title: The UK impact economy is worth £428bn. Here's what it does
item.description: The impact economy is worth an estimated £428bn to the UK, comparable to the entire manufacturing sector – and it's broader than you think.

item.title: Water bills are rising and thousands are planning not to pay
item.description: The Take Back Water campaign has seen thousands of people vow they will not pay their water bill until the government returns water to public ownership.

item.title: Young Once: A Life Less Heavy by Nigel Planer book review
item.description: Smart, funny, self-aware and likeable, Nigel Planer is an engaging raconteur with anecdotes to spare in Young Once: A Life Less Heavy

item.title: After the Flood: Inside Bob Dylan’s Memory Palace book review
item.description: After the Flood: Inside Bob Dylan’s Memory Palace argues that Dylan's genius didn’t fade, but evolved and mutated in fascinating ways.

item.title: How UK could save money by giving out cash – not cutting benefits
item.description: Benefit cuts and sanctions are often part of government reforms to save money – but studies show free cash handouts could be more effective.
